meaning: to make more effort than is required or expected in order to achieve a goal
literal_translation: esforzarse más de lo que se espera
example: I went the extra mile on my project by interviewing five more users.
origin: Probably from the image of walking one more mile beyond what is required; the exact origin is unclear.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to walk a long distance on foot
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal sense of the words; the idiom is figurative and refers to extra effort, not walking.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to finish a task later than planned
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about doing more than necessary, not about being late or delayed.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse to help other people
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes extra effort and generosity, so refusing to help is the opposite of its meaning.

explanation: 'Go the extra mile' means to make more effort than is required to achieve a goal. It is useful when describing your project in an oral exam.
